_about: Public-domain George Henry Gerberding (1847-1927), Lutheran pastor and professor at Chicago Lutheran Seminary, for the Word Hoard: The Way of Salvation in the Lutheran Church, New Testament Conversions, The Lutheran Pastor, the Life and Letters of W. A. Passavant, The Lutheran Church in the Country, his sketch of R. F. Weidner, What's Wrong with the World?, The Priesthood of Believers, Lutheran Fundamentals, and Reminiscent Reflections of a Youthful Octogenarian. Texts are from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 114 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

gerberding-way-salvation: The way of salvation in the Lutheran church (Philadelphia, Pa., Pub. for the author, Lutheran publication society, 1887)
gerberding-nt-conversions: New Testament conversions : a series of sermons (Philadelphia, Pa. : Pub. for the author, Lutheran publication society, 1889)
gerberding-lutheran-pastor: The Lutheran pastor (Philadelphia, Pa. : Lutheran Publication Society, 1902)
gerberding-passavant: Life and letters of W. A. Passavant, D. D (Greenville, Pa., The Young Lutheran co., 1906)
gerberding-country: The Lutheran church in the country; a study, an explanation, an attempted solution (Philadelphia, General council publication board, 1916)
gerberding-weidner: R. F. Weidner, D.D. LL.D. : a character sketch, an appreciation, a tribute (Waverly, Iowa : Wartburg Press, 1916)
gerberding-whats-wrong: What's Wrong with the World?: A Candid Inquiry Into the Underlying Spirit (Gerberding, 1919)
gerberding-priesthood: The Priesthood of Believers in Its Relation to Inner Mission Work of (The Inner Mission Boardof the United LutheranChurch in America, 1920)
gerberding-fundamentals: Lutheran fundamentals, a simple system of Scripture truth with applications for the common man (Rock Island, Ill. : Augustana Book Concern, 1925)
gerberding-reminiscent: Reminiscent reflections of a youthful octogenarian (Minneapolis, Minn. : Augsburg publishing house, 1928)
